packet.headline_seed: Russian attacks kill six as Ukraine targets Black Sea oil tankers
packet.description_seed: Overnight Russia attacked sites in Odesa and Sumy, while Ukraine attacked 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea.

what: Russian attacks kill six as Ukraine targets Black Sea oil tankers

clean_source_blocks.text: Overnight Russia attacked sites in Odesa and Sumy, while Ukraine attacked 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea.

He added that a non-residential building and a gas pipeline were also hit. In its statement, Russia claimed to have targeted sites involved in the manufacture of military hardware, and the transport of cargo. Russia's attacks in recent days have targeted Ukraine's deepwater Black Sea ports in the wider Odesa area, which handle much of the country's grain and other cargo and are vital to its wartime economy. Also overnight, Ukraine said its drones hit 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea. It follows intensive attacks on Russian ships in the Sea of Azov, which sits between Crimea, Ukraine's eastern coastline, and Russia. The Ukrainian attacks have forced Russia, the world's top grain exporter, to restrict shipping in the Sea of Azov - a route that handles about a quarter of its grain exports, according to news agency Reuters.

Editor's note: This is a developing story and is being updated. Ukraine has struck two major Russian oil refineries, a ship-loading area, several vessels, and other military and logistics targets overnight, Ukraine's General Staff said on July 14. The Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex in Russia's Republic of Bashkortostan and the Afipsky oil refinery in Russia's Krasnodar Krai came under Ukrainian attack overnight on July 14, the General Staff said. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the facility in Bashkortostan was located about 1,300 kilometers (810 miles) from the front line, while the refinery near the village of Afipsky was about 400 kilometers (250 miles) away. The Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex is one of Russia's largest oil refining and petrochemical facilities, with a designed annual processing capacity of about 10 million metric tons of oil, according to the General Staff.

Russian attacks overnight into Wednesday hit a residential building in Odesa Three people have been killed following an overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port of Odesa, according to a local official. Governor of Odesa region Oleh Kiper said the "massive" drone and missile strike marked the fifth day in which Russia has attacked the region. The Russian ministry of defence said it had deliberately targeted port infrastructure, "used for the unloading of petroleum, oil, and lubricants". The attacks come as European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visits Kyiv to discuss co-operation between European and Ukrainian defence industries. Writing on Telegram, Kiper accused Russia of deliberately targeting the civilian population, as well as industrial and port infrastructure in the area. He said residents were killed and injured when a Russian missile struck a multi-storey residential building.

TEMPO.CO, Jakarta - A Russian attack has killed at least three people and wounded 17 others in Ukraine's northern Sumy region, DW reported.

Regional Governor Oleh Hryhorov said Russian forces launched six guided aerial bombs during the daytime assault.

One bomb struck near medical facilities, while others appeared to hit infrastructure, according to preliminary information.

"Three people were killed and 17 were wounded," Hryhorov said.

He said a woman and a man were among those killed. A third victim suffered such severe injuries that authorities were initially unable to determine the person's gender.

Russian forces have struck port and residential infrastructure across Ukraine's southern Odesa and Mykolaiv regions, killing three people and injuring at least four others.

The attack on Odesa hit residential buildings, killing three people and leaving three more with moderate injuries, city military administration chief Serhiy Lysak said on Telegram. The wounded were taken to the hospital.

Odesa regional Governor Oleh Kiper said Russia's "massive" combined drone and missile assault had continued for a fifth consecutive day, targeting civilian, industrial and port infrastructure.

In the neighboring Mykolaiv region, a Russian drone strike on port facilities injured one man early on Wednesday, regional Governor Vitaliy Kim said.

Russia's Defense Ministry confirmed carrying out a combined attack on the Odesa region using air-launched precision weapons and combat drones.

Moscow said it targeted fuel storage tanks and loading facilities allegedly used by the Ukrainian military at the ports of Odesa and Chornomorsk, as well as a drone production site.

Odesa has repeatedly come under Russian attack because of its strategic role as a major Black Sea port. Civilians have frequently been killed in strikes on the city since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

payload.title: Venäjän iskuissa kuusi kuollutta – Ukraina hyökkäsi venäläisaluksia ja öljynjalostamoja vastaan
payload.summary: Venäjän yön yli jatkuneissa iskuissa Ukrainaan kuoli kuusi ihmistä. Ukraina puolestaan ilmoitti iskeneensä 20 venäläisalukseen Mustallamerellä sekä kahteen suureen öljynjalostamoon Venäjällä.
payload.content:
Venäjän Odesaan ja Sumyyn tekemissä yön yli jatkuneissa iskuissa kuoli yhteensä kuusi ihmistä. Ukraina ilmoitti samaan aikaan iskeneensä lennokeilla 20 venäläisalukseen Mustallamerellä sekä öljynjalostamoihin ja muihin sotilaallisiin ja logistisiin kohteisiin Venäjällä.

Asuinrakennukseen osui Odesassa

Odesan alueen kuvernöörin Oleh Kiperin mukaan kolme ihmistä kuoli Venäjän iskussa Mustanmeren rannalla sijaitsevaan satamakaupunkiin. Ohjus osui kerrostaloon, minkä seurauksena ihmisiä myös loukkaantui. Lisäksi vaurioita aiheutui muulle rakennukselle ja kaasuputkelle. Kiper kuvaili lennokki- ja ohjusiskua laajaksi. Hänen mukaansa Venäjä oli hyökännyt Odesan alueelle viitenä peräkkäisenä päivänä ja kohdistanut iskuja siviilien lisäksi teollisuus- ja satamainfrastruktuuriin. Venäjän puolustusministeriö ilmoitti iskeneensä satamainfrastruktuuriin, jota sen mukaan käytettiin polttoaineiden ja voiteluaineiden purkamiseen. Venäjä kertoi kohdistaneensa hyökkäyksiä myös sotilaskaluston valmistukseen ja rahdin kuljettamiseen liittyviin kohteisiin. Odesan alueen syväsatamat käsittelevät huomattavan osan Ukrainan viljasta ja muusta rahdista. Siksi ne ovat tärkeitä maan sodanaikaiselle taloudelle. Iskut tapahtuivat Euroopan komission puheenjohtajan Ursula von der Leyenin vieraillessa Kiovassa keskustelemassa Euroopan ja Ukrainan puolustusteollisuuden yhteistyöstä.

Ukraina ilmoitti laajoista vastaiskuista

Ukraina kertoi lennokkiensa osuneen yön aikana 20 venäläisalukseen Mustallamerellä. Tätä olivat edeltäneet voimakkaat hyökkäykset venäläisiä aluksia vastaan Asovanmerellä. Hyökkäysten seurauksena Venäjä on rajoittanut liikennettä reitillä, jonka kautta kulkee noin neljännes maan viljanviennistä. Ukrainan yleisesikunnan mukaan iskuja tehtiin myös Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat -laitokseen Baškortostanissa ja Afipskin öljynjalostamoon Krasnodarin alueella. Presidentti Volodymyr Zelenskyin mukaan Baškortostanin kohde sijaitsee noin 1 300 kilometrin ja Afipskin jalostamo noin 400 kilometrin päässä rintamasta. Baškortostanin laitos kuuluu Venäjän suurimpiin öljynjalostus- ja petrokemian tuotantokeskuksiin. Sen suunniteltu vuotuinen käsittelykapasiteetti on noin kymmenen miljoonaa tonnia öljyä. Sodan osapuolten kaikkia tietoja iskujen kohteista ja vaikutuksista ei ole vahvistettu riippumattomasti.
summary_bullets: Venäjän iskuissa Odesaan ja Sumyyn kuoli yhteensä kuusi ihmistä.
Ukrainan mukaan lennokki-iskut kohdistuivat myös kahteen suureen venäläiseen öljynjalostamoon.
payload.journalist_note: Kuuden kuolonuhrin kokonaismäärä sisältyy aineiston pääväitteeseen, mutta tarkempi lähdeaineisto yksilöi vain kolme Odesassa kuollutta. Osapuolten ilmoitukset sotilaskohteisiin tehdyistä iskuista vaativat riippumatonta vahvistusta.

Baškortostanin laitos kuuluu Venäjän suurimpiin öljynjalostus- ja petrokemian tuotantokeskuksiin. Sen suunniteltu vuotuinen käsittelykapasiteetti on noin kymmenen miljoonaa tonnia öljyä. Sodan osapuolten kaikkia tietoja iskujen kohteista ja vaikutuksista ei ole vahvistettu riippumattomasti.

Overnight Russia attacked sites in Odesa and Sumy, while Ukraine attacked 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea.

He added that a non-residential building and a gas pipeline were also hit. In its statement, Russia claimed to have targeted sites involved in the manufacture of military hardware, and the transport of cargo. Russia's attacks in recent days have targeted Ukraine's deepwater Black Sea ports in the wider Odesa area, which handle much of the country's grain and other cargo and are vital to its wartime economy. Also overnight, Ukraine said its drones hit 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea. It follows intensive attacks on Russian ships in the Sea of Azov, which sits between Crimea, Ukraine's eastern coastline, and Russia. The Ukrainian attacks have forced Russia, the world's top grain exporter, to restrict shipping in the Sea of Azov - a route that handles about a quarter of its grain exports, according to news agency Reuters.

Editor's note: This is a developing story and is being updated. Ukraine has struck two major Russian oil refineries, a ship-loading area, several vessels, and other military and logistics targets overnight, Ukraine's General Staff said on July 14. The Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex in Russia's Republic of Bashkortostan and the Afipsky oil refinery in Russia's Krasnodar Krai came under Ukrainian attack overnight on July 14, the General Staff said. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the facility in Bashkortostan was located about 1,300 kilometers (810 miles) from the front line, while the refinery near the village of Afipsky was about 400 kilometers (250 miles) away. The Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat complex is one of Russia's largest oil refining and petrochemical facilities, with a designed annual processing capacity of about 10 million metric tons of oil, according to the General Staff.

Russian attacks overnight into Wednesday hit a residential building in Odesa Three people have been killed following an overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port of Odesa, according to a local official. Governor of Odesa region Oleh Kiper said the "massive" drone and missile strike marked the fifth day in which Russia has attacked the region. The Russian ministry of defence said it had deliberately targeted port infrastructure, "used for the unloading of petroleum, oil, and lubricants". The attacks come as European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visits Kyiv to discuss co-operation between European and Ukrainian defence industries. Writing on Telegram, Kiper accused Russia of deliberately targeting the civilian population, as well as industrial and port infrastructure in the area. He said residents were killed and injured when a Russian missile struck a multi-storey residential building.
